extracted.intended_audience: corporate clients, in-house counsel, and stakeholders seeking representation or guidance in ITC Section 337 (U.S. International Trade Commission) patent enforcement/defense matters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on capabilities and practical standards for representing parties in U.S. International Trade Commission (Section 337) investigations, emphasizing the skills, experience, and operational requirements needed for high‑stakes, fast-paced ITC patent disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle high‑stakes, fast-moving ITC litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) has become a key forum for high-stakes global intellectual property disputes. The cases move fast and the remedy is powerful. There is little room for learning on the job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should be experienced and prepared from the outset; clients need lawyers who can operate under aggressive timelines and with an understanding that remedies (e.g., exclusion orders) can have immediate, substantial business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid discovery and compressed schedule capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery lasts only a few months and the case is brought to trial in eight to 10 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must be able to manage accelerated discovery, rapid document review, expedited expert work, and trial preparation. Litigation strategy should be developed early to meet compressed deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience inside the ITC and related agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Team includes a former Chairman and Commissioner of the ITC; former lawyers from the crucial regulatory and enforcement authorities, including the ITC Office of General Counsel, and the ITC Office of Unfair Import Investigation (OUII); and a former senior official from the Office of United States Trade Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior service inside the ITC, OUII, OGC, or USTR provides valuable procedural and substantive insight into investigations, agency decision-making, and enforcement—advantages in planning and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated international IP counseling, litigation, and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing on leading patent litigation, international trade, and government relations practices, Covington provides effective guidance through integrated international IP counseling, litigation, and enforcement for business‑critical issues before the ITC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective representation requires coordination across patent litigation, customs/enforcement, and government-relations capabilities to address global commercial and regulatory dimensions of Section 337 matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient staffing depth and global coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 60 lawyers firm-wide with significant experience in this area; depth necessary to staff even the most challenging cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firms should demonstrate capacity to assemble multi-discipline teams, provide sustained resourcing through aggressive schedules, and cover cross-border issues (e.g., Asia practice leadership).

rubrics_metrics.name: Early development of trial-ready litigation strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel with years of experience inside the ITC’s courtrooms and before its Administrative Law Judges develop litigation strategy at the earliest stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a greater share of Section 337 cases go to trial versus district‑court patent cases, teams must assume trial is likely and prepare accordingly (witnesses, demonstratives, evidentiary rulings, and ALJ practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-order enforcement and customs coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawyers routinely remain involved after an order issues, and have significant practical experience working with customs departments and the ITC to properly implement and enforce both limited and general exclusion orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective ITC practice includes hands-on experience implementing exclusion orders at the border, interfacing with customs authorities, and managing enforcement logistics to ensure orders achieve intended commercial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistance minimizing business impact after exclusion orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant experience assisting companies confronted with an exclusion order, including companies represented by different counsel during the investigation, to ensure that any business impact after the ITC case ends is minimized to the greatest extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel should offer practical remediation, transition support, licensing, redesign/variants counselling, and enforcement-challenge strategies to reduce downstream commercial harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience representing both complainant and respondent perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of the nuances of real-world enforcement from both the complainant and the respondent’s perspective translates directly into increased efficiency in preparation and case management, more effective results-focused litigation strategy, and better business outcomes at the border after an exclusion order issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual-perspective experience helps anticipate opponent strategies, design effective defenses or enforcement plans, and optimize case management and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proven track record and longevity in Section 337 practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Have appeared in over 100 Section 337 cases spanning nearly 30 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demonstrated history of handling many Section 337 matters over time indicates institutional knowledge, precedent familiarity, and tested methodologies for success in the forum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized qualifications and leadership in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Firm attorneys include Fellows of the American College of Trial Lawyers, past presidents/vice chairs of relevant trial lawyer associations, and practitioners recognized by Chambers, Legal 500, IAM, and other rankings/awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External recognition and leadership roles are signals of expertise and reputation that clients may rely on when selecting counsel for high‑stakes ITC matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and leveraging powerful ITC remedies (exclusion orders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 337 cases ... the remedy is powerful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel must understand the scope, implementation, and limits of exclusion and cease‑and‑desist-type remedies and plan both enforcement and defense strategies with their immediate commercial consequences in mind.
